meta.title: Brindlemere: The Cinder King
meta.note: x grows to the east, y to the south; zone 0,0 is the north-west corner. The sea lies beyond the west edge.
meta.goal: Slay Vharaxis, the Cinder King, on Mount Cindermaw and bring the news home to Elder Maren.
story: Three hundred years ago the red dragon Vharaxis burnt the kingdom of Thornreach in one night.
A dwarf-forged blade of star-iron and glacier ice, Winter's Tooth, drove him into Mount Cindermaw. The blade broke; the Cindergate was built to seal him in.
Now a cult, the Ashen Choir, sings to wake him. It starts with a bell tolling under a village graveyard.
Someone opened Thornreach's gates that night. No one ever learned who.

features: the sea to the west and north

zones.name: Rimewater Glacier
zones.blurb: A river of blue ice. Something vast sleeps in its heart.
features: the ice cave of the white wyrm

zones.name: Ashfall Reach
zones.blurb: Grey ash falls like snow on a burnt plain.

zones.name: Mount Cindermaw
zones.blurb: The fire mountain. The Cinder King's hoard lies in its throat.

zones.name: Gullcry Cliffs
zones.blurb: White cliffs loud with seabirds, and an old lighthouse.

zones.name: Pinewatch

zones.name: Hollowhorn Hills

zones.name: Greywether Moor

npcs.name: Elder Maren
npcs.title: village elder (your round 3 quest giver)
lines: Brindlemere has stood by its pond for three hundred years.
My grandmother saw the red wyrm cross the sky. I pray I never do.

npcs.name: Orwyn
npcs.title: warden of the pond (your round 1 villager)
lines: The pond is older than the village. They say a star fell into it once.
Six roads leave Aldermoor's heart. All of them start at our gate.

npcs.name: Pella Thrushcombe
npcs.title: innkeeper of the Brass Kettle
lines: A bed at the Brass Kettle mends any wound.
Travellers say the heath road is thick with Redcaps this year.

npcs.name: Mabel Fenn
npcs.title: general store
lines: Rope, rations, a blade if you must. Coin first, dear.
My sister Greta hunts in Pinewatch. Tell her to write.

npcs.name: Hale
npcs.title: woodsman (your round 3 helper)
lines: Thornwood was a royal hunting park before the kings fell.
Wolves I can handle. It is the goblins that worry me.

npcs.name: Brother Tobin
npcs.title: gravekeeper (your round 3 gravekeeper)
lines: I have buried four generations of Brindlemere here.
The old kings lie south-east, in the Barrows. They sleep worse than my flock.

npcs.name: Ilsabet Quill
npcs.title: Loremistress of Highmarrow
lines: Every road in Aldermoor crosses at Highmarrow. So does every rumour.
Thornreach fell in a single night of fire. The dragon was called Vharaxis.
A blade named Winter's Tooth drove him into the mountain. It broke doing so.

npcs.name: Osric Hammerfall
npcs.title: armourer
lines: Good steel is cheaper than a funeral.
The dwarves of Karn Doruhl taught my father. I still cannot match them.

npcs.name: Bram Tolliver
npcs.title: caravan master
lines: Three wagons lost on the hill road this month. Three!
Goblins take a toll. Bugbears take the wagon.

npcs.name: Wick the Crier
npcs.title: town crier
lines: Hear ye! The Ashen Choir are outlaws by order of the council!
Hear ye! Ash fell on the north fields again last night!

npcs.name: Dunmore Pell
npcs.title: harbourmaster
lines: No ship leaves Saltmere without my mark in the book.
The old lighthouse on Gullcry went dark the night the harpies came.

npcs.name: Captain Ines Marlow
npcs.title: ship's chandler
lines: If it floats, burns or ties a knot, I sell it.
Wrecker's Coast earned its name. Those lights are no lighthouse.

npcs.name: Nan Saltwhistle
npcs.title: net mender
lines: My husband fished the ice shore once. He came back with white hair.
A hag keeps a cave down the coast. She buys what the sea takes.

npcs.name: Old Corwin
npcs.title: lighthouse keeper
lines: Forty years I kept the lamp. Then they stole the lens.
On a clear day you can see the ice in the north from the lamp room.

npcs.name: Greta Fenn
npcs.title: huntress
lines: The watchtower was built to warn of giants. Nobody is left to light it.
A wolf the size of a pony leads the pack now. We call him Greymaw.

npcs.name: Ulf the Quiet
npcs.title: hermit
lines: The pines remember the dragon. Look how they lean away from the east.

npcs.name: Tam Oatley
npcs.title: farmer
lines: Best barley in Aldermoor, when something is not eating the shepherds.
The ground shook under the east field. Then the sheep were gone.

npcs.name: Joss the Miller
npcs.title: miller
lines: Ash in the flour again. It blows down from the north-east.
My mill has ground corn for Highmarrow since the kings.

npcs.name: Sergeant Brakenridge
npcs.title: road warden
lines: Goblins dig, hobgoblins drill, bugbears do as they please.
Hold the hill road and you hold the way to the dwarves.

npcs.name: Widow Harrow
npcs.title: peat cutter
lines: Never follow the lights on the moor. My Edmund did.
The fog comes from the barrows, whatever the wise say.

npcs.name: Brakka Ironvein
npcs.title: Forgemaster of Karn Doruhl
lines: Karn Doruhl has never fallen. The dragon tried once.
My forebears forged Winter's Tooth from a fallen star and glacier ice.
Star-iron does not melt in common fire. It wants a wyrm's cold.

npcs.name: Thrain Coppervein
npcs.title: hold smith
lines: Dwarf-made. It will outlive you, and I mean that kindly.
We sell to tall folk again since the ash began to fall.

npcs.name: Durgan Kettlehelm
npcs.title: gate captain
lines: Frost giants took my brother's patrol for ransom.
The pass east is called Stonejaw. It bites.

npcs.name: Sigrun Frostmane
npcs.title: ice hunter
lines: The glacier sings before it cracks. Listen, and live.
Hoarfang is young, as wyrms go. That only makes him hungry.

npcs.name: Old Yrsa
npcs.title: bone carver
lines: My people walked here over the ice, before there were kings.
White bears fear fire. White wolves do not.

npcs.name: Garn Stonehand
npcs.title: prospector
lines: A star fell in this pass when my grandfather was a lad.
Two-headed Grum-and-Gorl argues with himself. Loudly. Follow the noise.

npcs.name: Ser Aldric Thorne
npcs.title: last knight of Thornreach
lines: My order guarded these halls. I guard their dust.
A pale lady came to court the night before the fire. She still walks, far to the south-east.

npcs.name: Penn Dewberry
npcs.title: antiquarian
lines: Thornreach, year 612: 'The sky is red. The king will not flee.'
The Cindergate was built to keep the dragon in. Mark that: in.

npcs.name: Zafira al-Sahra
npcs.title: the Loremistress's agent
lines: The spire throws no shadow at noon. The desert folk call it the Needle.
The Choir buys silence with gold and pays the rest in ash.

npcs.name: Yusra of the Blue Tent
npcs.title: apothecary
lines: Water is free. Everything else has a price.
Drink before you are thirsty. Heal before you are dying.

npcs.name: Hakim Nour
npcs.title: healer
lines: Scorpion venom kills. A drop of it, prepared well, cures.
The salt flats south-east are white as bone and twice as dead.

npcs.name: Idris
npcs.title: caravan guide
lines: The dunes sing when the wind is right. Do not sing back.
A woman with a lion's body offers water out here. Refuse it.

npcs.name: Speaker Sszath
npcs.title: voice of the marsh folk
lines: We were here before the warm-bloods. We will be here after.
The Moon Shrine was ours to tend. Now a black wyrmling fouls its well.

npcs.name: Issa Reedweaver
npcs.title: basket maker
lines: The fen gives reeds, eels and fever. Take two of the three.
The marsh folk speak slowly. They are never wrong about the weather.

npcs.name: Ferryman Odd
npcs.title: ferryman
lines: A copper to cross, when there is a bridge left to cross to.
The troll grows back what you cut off. Burn it.

npcs.name: The Mud Pilgrim
npcs.title: pilgrim
lines: The moon drowned here. I am looking for it.
Count your steps in Blackmire. The mire counts them too.

npcs.name: Hob Ashby
npcs.title: woodcutter
lines: Leaves fall here all year and the trees never go bare. Explain that.
Something big sleeps in the hollow oak. It hoots. It also growls.

npcs.name: Sister Averil
npcs.title: hermit of the barrow chapel
lines: Seven kings lie in seven mounds. I pray over six.
The seventh wears his circlet still, and walks.

npcs.name: Professor Lysander Brock
npcs.title: explorer
lines: Remarkable flora. Everything here is trying to eat everything else.
The statues at Serpent's Rest are too good. No sculptor carves fear like that.

npcs.name: Nessa Quickfingers
npcs.title: tomb robber
lines: I am an historian. With a crowbar.
The Sun-King took his whole court into the dark with him.

npcs.name: Vex
npcs.title: kobold trader
lines: Vex sells nothing today. Vex only warns: wyvern nests up high.
Big-folk get lost in red rock. Kobolds never lost.

npcs.name: Dag Whitehand
npcs.title: salt prospector
lines: Salt is white gold. The land sharks agree, sadly.
If the ground hums, stand still. If it roars, run.

npcs.name: Kestrel
npcs.title: ranger scout
lines: Gnolls follow the ash. They think the dragon is a god.
Do not look at the lizard with eight legs. Look at its shadow.

npcs.name: Corin Ashwalker
npcs.title: cult deserter
lines: I sang with the Choir. Then I saw what we were singing to.
The Cantor sings. Someone else writes the song.

npcs.name: The Last Warden
npcs.title: ghostly gate warden
lines: We built the gate to hold him in. We held. We hold.
The song has cracked it. It will fail within days, with you or without you.
Open it, and you must finish him. Fire will not harm him. Bring winter.

npcs.name: Acolyte Miren
npcs.title: last acolyte of the Moon
lines: The Moon Stone remembers everything spoken before it.
The Choir asked it one question: where does the Cinder King sleep?
Then another came, alone, and asked a second. I heard no breath between the words.

npcs.name: Quiet Tomas
npcs.title: a man who whispers
lines: Keep your voice down. She hunts by sound when her eyes are closed.
A mirror. I would trade my boots for a mirror.

npcs.name: Old Seti
npcs.title: tomb guide
lines: I guided scholars here. Now I guide no one, and I am richer for it.
The singing below never stops. It is not a happy song.
They bow to someone else. Someone who never comes by day.

npcs.name: Mirelle Starwatch
npcs.title: astrologer
lines: The star that fell here was the twin of the one in the dwarves' pass.
The Countess keeps her shutters shut by day. She says the ash suits her.

npcs.name: Finn the Drover
npcs.title: cattle drover
lines: Warm wind from the south means rain. From the north-east, ash.
Orcs raid the downs every autumn. This year they came early.

npcs.name: Gibbet Jack
npcs.title: repentant bandit
lines: I rode with the Redcaps till the hooded ones started paying.
Garrick keeps his ledger in his coat. He trusts nobody. Wise man.

npcs.name: Tilly Wrack
npcs.title: beachcomber
lines: Finders keepers. That is the law of the coast.
A black sloop broke up on the rocks last moon. Its crew wore hoods.

quest_items.name: Healing Draught
quest_items.desc: Your round 3 potion: restores 2d4+2 HP. Keep it working as it is.

quest_items.name: Crypt Key
quest_items.desc: Opens the gate of the Hollow Crypt. (round 3)

quest_items.name: Gravecaller's Bell
quest_items.desc: The bell that woke the dead. It bears a founder's mark. (round 3)

quest_items.name: Ashen Ledger
quest_items.desc: The Redcaps' accounts: payments from 'the Choir'.

quest_items.name: Ashen Sigil
quest_items.desc: A seal of black glass with a crescent moon scratched out.

quest_items.name: Moonstone Rubbing
quest_items.desc: A charcoal rubbing of the Moon Stone's last answer.

quest_items.name: Letter of Passage
quest_items.desc: The Loremistress's letter to the dwarves.

quest_items.name: Star-iron Ingot
quest_items.desc: Metal from a fallen star. Cold to the touch.

quest_items.name: Unquenched Blade
quest_items.desc: Winter's Tooth, reforged but not yet quenched.

quest_items.name: Heart of Rime
quest_items.desc: A shard of ice that never melts, from the white wyrm's lair.

quest_items.name: Cinder Key
quest_items.desc: A key of black iron, warm as a hearthstone.

quest_items.name: Pale Note
quest_items.desc: A note in a pale, old-fashioned hand, signed V.

quest_items.name: Lighthouse Lens
quest_items.desc: The stolen lens of the Gullcry light.

quest_items.name: Oldking's Circlet
quest_items.desc: A plain iron circlet, very cold.

quest_items.name: Canopic Jar
quest_items.desc: A sealed jar from the Sun-King's pyramid.

main.name: The Restless Crypt
main.summary: The dead stir under Thornwood. (This is your round 3 quest: keep it working exactly as it is; quest.stage 0-6 are these six steps.)

steps.log: Talk to Elder Maren in Brindlemere.
pages: The dead do not rest. A bell tolls under Thornwood every night.
Find Brother Tobin at the cemetery, east through the gate. Take this.

steps.log: Find Brother Tobin at the cemetery in Thornwood.
pages: A hooded man, the Gravecaller, went into the crypt. I locked the gate behind him.
The key is in the chest in the north glade.

steps.name: Old chest
steps.log: Open the chest in the north glade.
pages: You pull the red cord and the chest opens. You got the Crypt Key!

steps.name: Crypt gate
steps.log: Unlock the crypt gate with the key.
pages: The key turns and the gate swings open. The old key crumbles to rust.

steps.log: Defeat the Gravecaller in the crypt.
Take the bell back to Elder Maren.
pages: The Gravecaller's bell! Then it is over. Thank you.

main.name: The Bell's Maker
main.summary: The bell bears a founder's mark. Whose?

steps.log: Ask Elder Maren about the bell.
pages: Look at the mark under the rim: a ring of ash. I have never seen it.
Take the road north-east to Highmarrow. Loremistress Ilsabet Quill will know it.

steps.log: Show the bell to Ilsabet Quill in Highmarrow.
pages: The Ashen Choir. A cult I had hoped was only a story.
Their gold goes through the Redcap bandits on Gallows Heath, east of here. Bring me Garrick Redcap's ledger.
One of them left the gang: Gibbet Jack. He still camps on the heath, and he talks.

steps.log: Defeat Garrick Redcap on Gallows Heath.
Bring the ledger to Ilsabet Quill.
pages: Payments every month. Cargo by sea.
And look at the coin. Pale silver, Thornreach mint. Nobody has struck that in three hundred years.

main.name: Salt and Shadow
main.summary: The Choir ships something through Saltmere.

steps.log: Ask Ilsabet Quill what the ledger says.
pages: The cargo landed at Saltmere, on the west coast. Harbourmaster Dunmore Pell keeps the book.
Follow the cargo. I want to know what they dug up.

steps.log: Speak to Harbourmaster Dunmore Pell in Saltmere.
pages: A black sloop, hooded crew. She never made port: wrecked a little south, on Wrecker's Coast.
That same night the Gullcry lamp went dark. I do not believe in chance.
The hag they call Old Mother Brine takes whatever washes up there.

steps.log: Defeat Old Mother Brine on Wrecker's Coast.

steps.name: Sealed crate
steps.log: Open the Choir's crate in the hag's cave.
pages: Under wet straw lies a seal of black glass. You got the Ashen Sigil.

steps.log: Bring the sigil to Ilsabet Quill.
pages: A moon, scratched out. This was pried from the Moon Shrine in the southern mire.

main.name: The Drowned Shrine
main.summary: What did the Choir ask the Moon Stone?

steps.log: Ask Ilsabet Quill about the Moon Shrine.
pages: The shrine lies drowned in the far south-west. The marsh folk of Willowfen tend it.
Find their Speaker, Sszath. Be polite. They remember rudeness for generations.

steps.log: Find Speaker Sszath in Willowfen.
pages: The hooded ones left a black wyrmling in the shrine's well. We call it Mirefang.
Kill it, warm-blood, and the Moon Stone will speak to you.
One acolyte still keeps the shrine. Miren heard what the hooded ones asked.

steps.log: Slay Mirefang at the Drowned Shrine.

steps.name: The Moon Stone
steps.log: Read the Moon Stone.
pages: Words rise in the stone: 'He sleeps under Cindermaw. The song will wake him.'
Fainter words below, from a second voice with no breath: 'When will the sky go dark?'
You take a rubbing of the Moon Stone.

steps.log: Bring the rubbing to Ilsabet Quill.
pages: Vharaxis. They mean to wake the Cinder King.
Fire cannot hurt him. One blade did: Winter's Tooth. And it broke doing it.
The only weapon that ever bit him lies in pieces. And who asks when the sky goes dark?

main.name: The Dwarven Road
main.summary: Winter's Tooth must be forged again.

steps.log: Ask Ilsabet Quill about Winter's Tooth.
pages: The dwarves of Karn Doruhl made it, far to the north. Forgemaster Brakka Ironvein keeps the shards.
Take my letter, or she will not even open the gate.

steps.log: Bring the letter to Brakka Ironvein in Karn Doruhl.
pages: Quill's hand. Hm. I can forge it again, but not from common iron.
A star fell in Stonejaw Pass, east of here. Bring me star-iron. Mind the ettin.

steps.log: Defeat the ettin Grum-and-Gorl in Stonejaw Pass.

steps.name: Star-iron vein
steps.log: Dig star-iron from the fallen star.
pages: You pry a lump of blue-black metal from the rock. You got a Star-iron Ingot.

steps.log: Bring the star-iron to Brakka Ironvein.
pages: Star-iron! I have waited my whole life to work this.
Mind, my forge burns red without coal these days. Something under the mountain is breathing.

main.name: Winter's Tooth
main.summary: The blade must be quenched in a wyrm's cold.

steps.log: Ask Brakka Ironvein about the blade.
pages: The blade is forged, but it is only steel until it is quenched in true cold.
A white wyrm lairs in the glacier to the west. Sigrun Frostmane hunts on the shore beyond. Ask her.

steps.log: Find Sigrun Frostmane on Frostfang Shore.
pages: Hoarfang's cave is in the heart of the Rimewater, east of here.
In his nest lies ice that never melts. That is your quench.

steps.log: Slay Hoarfang in Rimewater Glacier.
Bring the Heart of Rime to Brakka Ironvein.
pages: Stand back. ... There. Winter's Tooth bites again.
A smith cannot march. But a smith can arm the one who does. Go.

main.name: The Ashen Choir
main.summary: The Choir holds the key to the mountain. Who holds the Choir?

steps.log: Tell Ilsabet Quill the blade is whole.
pages: Then we strike first. The Choir sings in the Sepulchre of Sand, far to the east.
My agent Zafira waits at Sunspire Oasis. Go to her.

steps.log: Meet Zafira at Sunspire Oasis.
pages: Their High Cantor, Sereth Vane, wears the Cinder Key on a chain.
The Sepulchre is east of here. Old Seti sits at its door. He hears more than the Choir thinks.

steps.log: Defeat High Cantor Sereth Vane in the Sepulchre of Sand.
pages: Sereth Vane falls, still singing. There is no key on his chain.
'I was only the voice,' he whispers. 'She wrote the song.'

steps.name: The Choir's altar
steps.log: Take the Cinder Key from the altar.
pages: Among black candles lies a key of warm iron. Under it, a note in a pale hand.
'Bring it to me at dusk, Sereth. You are late. - V.'

steps.log: Bring the key and the note to Zafira.
pages: You have it! And this hand... V. Velda Mournshade. The countess who opened Thornreach's gates.
So she wrote the song. She does not want a king. She wants his ash: a sky dark enough to walk under.
Ser Aldric hunts her from the Thornreach Ruins. But the song was sung too long. Ash is falling in the north.

steps.log: Ask Zafira for the way to the mountain.
pages: North, through the badlands, stands the Cindergate. Beyond it, Mount Cindermaw.
He is waking. Take the key and Winter's Tooth. A warden still stands at the gate. Hear him.

steps.name: The Cindergate
steps.log: Open the Cindergate with the Cinder Key.
pages: The key burns white. The black gate grinds open on a road of ash.
The gate was built to hold him in. Now it stands open. There is no way left but through him.

steps.log: Slay Vharaxis, the Cinder King, on Mount Cindermaw.
pages: WHO WAKES THE CINDER KING? ... A blade of winter. I remember that sting.

steps.log: Go home to Brindlemere and tell Elder Maren.
pages: Look up. The ash has stopped. The sky is blue.
Tobin hung the old bell in the chapel. Tonight it rings for the living.
Brindlemere will sing of you for three hundred years more.

steps.log: Talk to Pella at the Brass Kettle.
pages: Something the size of a dog is in my cellar. It ate a ham. A whole ham!

steps.log: Kill the giant rat by the inn.
Tell Pella the cellar is safe.
pages: Bless you. Supper is on the house, and take this for the road.
Odd thing: it nested in a crate that is not mine. Stamped with a ring of ash.

steps.log: Talk to Tam Oatley in Larkspur Fields.
pages: My shepherd went to the east field and the field ate him. Burrows everywhere.

steps.log: Kill the ankheg under the east field.
Tell Tam Oatley.
pages: So that is what an ankheg looks like. My old bow is yours.

steps.log: Talk to Greta Fenn in Pinewatch.
pages: Greymaw leads the pack to the farms now. I cannot take him alone.
They came south in a hurry. Wolves do that when the north smells of smoke.

steps.log: Hunt Greymaw in Pinewatch.
Return to Greta Fenn.
pages: The pack will scatter. Here, I stitched this from better days.
If you pass Brindlemere, tell my sister Mabel I still owe her a letter.

steps.log: Talk to Old Corwin on Gullcry Cliffs.
pages: Harpies took my lens for their nest. Shiny, you see. Ships are dying for it.
The lamp went dark the very night a black sloop came up the coast.

steps.log: Defeat the harpy on the cliff.

steps.name: Harpy nest
steps.log: Take the lens from the nest.
pages: Among bones and feathers: the Lighthouse Lens.

steps.log: Bring the lens to Old Corwin.
pages: She shines! Saltmere will see her tonight.
No hooded ship lands unseen on this coast again.

steps.log: Talk to Bram Tolliver in Highmarrow.
pages: Chief Krug holds the hill road north of here. A bugbear. Make him let go of it.

steps.log: Defeat Chief Krug in the Hollowhorn Hills.
Return to Bram Tolliver.
pages: The road is open! Take a shield from my stock, and my thanks.
Krug's purse was full of pale silver. Who pays a bugbear to shut the dwarves' road?

steps.log: Talk to Sister Averil at the Oldking Barrows.
pages: The seventh king walks. He rose the night a bell first rang under Thornwood.
Lay him down, and bring me his circlet to bless.

steps.log: Defeat the Barrow King.

steps.name: The seventh mound
steps.log: Take the circlet from the mound.
pages: Cold iron in cold earth. You got the Oldking's Circlet.

steps.log: Bring the circlet to Sister Averil.
pages: Now I can pray over seven. This mace was made for work like yours.

steps.log: Talk to Hakim Nour at Sunspire Oasis.
pages: I need venom from a great scorpion of the salt flats, south-east. Fresh.

steps.log: Kill a giant scorpion on Scorpion Flats.
Bring the venom sac to Hakim Nour.
pages: Perfect. Two of these will become twenty cures. These are for you.
Choir pilgrims buy my cures and walk east. They never come back.

steps.log: Talk to Professor Brock in the Emerald Deep.
pages: My whole expedition stands in that temple to the east. As statues. Avenge them, would you?

steps.log: Defeat the medusa at Serpent's Rest.
Return to Professor Brock.
pages: Poor fellows. Take my thinking-band. I shall need a long holiday from thinking.

steps.log: Talk to Ferryman Odd in the Mangrove Maze.
pages: A troll took the bridge and charges more than I do. Burn it out.

steps.log: Defeat the troll at the bridge.
Return to Ferryman Odd.
pages: Ha! It dropped these when it burned. Too big for me.

steps.log: Talk to Nessa Quickfingers in the Bonewhite Wastes.
pages: I opened the pyramid. Something inside opened its eyes. I will split the take!

steps.name: The pyramid door
steps.log: Take the canopic jar from the pyramid.
pages: The jar is warm, and something inside it beats.

steps.log: Defeat Sun-King Tahemet.
Return to Nessa Quickfingers.
pages: You keep the sword. I am keeping my distance from pyramids.

steps.log: Talk to Durgan Kettlehelm in Karn Doruhl.
pages: Jarl Skaldi holds my brother's patrol on the glacier, west. We do not pay giants.
The giants raid because a white wyrm drove them off the high ice.

steps.log: Defeat Jarl Skaldi on Rimewater Glacier.
Return to Durgan Kettlehelm.
pages: They are home. This plate was my brother's gift to whoever freed him.

steps.log: Talk to Ser Aldric Thorne in the Thornreach Ruins.
pages: Countess Velda Mournshade smiled at our king and opened our gates to the fire.
Three hundred years, and she still wants the sky dark. She holds court in the crater, far south-east.

steps.log: Destroy Countess Mournshade in the Fallen Star Crater.
pages: 'Such a long walk in the sun, little hero. One more song and I would never hide again.'
The Countess falls to ash. The shutters of her manor bang open in the wind.

steps.log: Return to Ser Aldric Thorne.
pages: Thornreach is avenged. My order's last treasures are yours.
Three hundred years I kept this watch. Tonight I will sleep.
